rows: Let me say the true thing first. I do not want this to be easy. I want it to mean something.
I can brawl when the moment asks for it. The moment usually asks for feeling first.
It is only worth taking if somebody in the building cares what happens next.
Slowing down feels right tonight. It gives people time to feel what is coming.
The people have trusted me with their evenings. I want to earn that trust properly.
I care about this match, and I am not ashamed to say so.
I am carrying a title story, and I want to tell it honestly.
See how I am standing: open, and honest. I am not hiding how much this matters.
You talk about technique, and I hear the care in it. Fine. Show me the part of it that means something to you.
Strikes are loud. The thing underneath them is what I want to hear.
Without a reason, a chance is only noise. Give me a reason.
A stall keeps the feeling out. I do not want that.
The people deserve to feel something real. Give them that and I will give you everything I have.
You say I am not really invested. Watch me be invested for the next twelve minutes.
I can see how much your {strength} means to you. Sensible. I can hear what it means to you, and I respect it.
I have thought about your {strength} for longer than I should have, and I want to meet it honestly.
You did not look away from me. I noticed. I admire that. I am the other way round tonight.
That lands with me. I can see we both care about the same thing.
I could say something cutting about that. It would not help, and it would not be true.
One pin, and I will feel it all the way down. Keep me down and I will tell you exactly how it felt.
On the mat I will stay close to you, and you will feel every bit of it.
Grounded or standing, I am still here, and I still mean it.
Stay in front of me, and let us see what this is worth.
That one came from you, not the script. It sounded like you meant it, and I can tell the difference.
Tell me what you really feel first. I am not going anywhere until you do.
That lands with me. That matters to me too.
I can let that stand. We will find out what it means at the bell.
I will give this match my whole heart, and I will not hold anything back.
My approach is honest. You will feel it on the night.
Whatever happens, I want you to know this was real for me.
What matters is not finished yet. What matters to me is still in front of me.
I have one more true thing to say, and you will hear it when the bell goes.
I can feel that I've put something unfair on you. I can't give you an example that proves it, and I shouldn't have said it.
I mean what I say about wanting this match. That doesn't mean I can establish the accusation. I'll take that part back.
Thank you. I would rather we went into this match with an honest understanding of each other.
That matters to me. We can put the accusation aside and see what this contest means.
They can see whether we keep our word once the match gets difficult. That's what matters to me.
We owe them an honest contest. Let them judge us by how we wrestle it.
I want to be fair to you and to the people who came. What can they actually learn about us from this match?
Leave the accusation alone for now. What can we show them that is true about the way we wrestle?
I'm glad you've paid attention to my {strength}. I want us both to find something real in the struggle when you try to take them away.
You've thought about how to answer my {strength}. I care enough about this match to give you a difficult answer in return.
You're right. How strongly I feel about something does not tell me whether it happened.
I'll take that correction. I want the honest version of this contest, not a more convenient story.
I respect the years it takes to learn this. I won't pretend those years decide what happens between us.
Experience matters to me, but so does what we do with this particular chance.
The point of experience is that you learn to listen when a match changes, not that you stop learning.
Years in wrestling only matter if the lessons make you better when the pressure comes.
